resources.timing_overlap_caveat: This one-thread background CPU analysis may overlap ongoing inference; no inference or service operation was performed by this process.
resources.initial_interpreter_attempt: The system python lacked numpy and exited before numerical computation; successful analysis used the existing Heretic environment.

methods.representation: W = decoded Google BF16 cast to F16 and back to float32, matching the phase-1 export null; H = decoded Hauhau F16; Delta = H-W.
methods.operator: Delta_hat=-U M U^T W; U is rank-5 delta left subspace. M least squares uses ridge=(trace(Gram)/5)*1e-10 and pinv rcond=1e-12.
methods.rank5_floor: Approximate best rank-5 error uses the saved randomized-SVD U; no full SVD is performed. It is a numerical spectral-floor estimate, not a certified optimal residual.
methods.cross_layer_operator: Frobenius inner products computed in rank space: <U M U^T,V N V^T>=<M,(U^T V)N(U^T V)^T>. No dense output operator is formed.
methods.column_split: Separate even/odd training-only U and M fits, with reverse holdout; deterministic randomized SVD sketch12/power2/retained8 then first5. Splitting weight columns tests algebraic stability, not independent behavioral generalization.
methods.rounding: Compute prediction in float64, cast to float32, round to nearest-even BF16 with a tested bit conversion, then cast to F16 for the stored export representation. No rounding-aware fitting.
methods.rounding_caveat: Reduced residual after rounding is consistent with a low-rank edit followed by BF16 rounding; it does not identify the exact historical code path or recover exact factors.
methods.numeric_tolerance: Float64 reductions and rank-space algebra; negative error energy is tolerated only down to -1e-10*max(delta_energy,1) before clamping zero.
methods.identifiability: A general 2816x2816 left operator is underdetermined by a 2816x2112 weight matrix. Reported fits explicitly restrict the operator input and output to U.
methods.causality: Detected weight geometry does not establish refusal, RLHF, safety, model-quality effects, or transfer success on REDCELL.

conclusions.recoverability: The sampled late-layer weight differences support stable, layer-specific rank-5 output edits. This is algebraic recoverability of edit geometry, without a demonstrated behavioral interpretation.
conclusions.fit_and_spectral_floor: Rank-5 restricted fits leave 6.320–7.812% relative delta residual; the approximate rank-5 spectral floors are 6.236–7.710%. Between 95.95% and 97.73% of fit-error energy is already at the rank-5 spectral floor.
conclusions.column_split_stability: With both U and M learned only from training columns, reverse held-out relative residuals are 6.302–7.953%; the lowest principal cosine between the two training subspaces is 0.999899. These are weight-column checks, not behavioral tests.
conclusions.operator_eigenvalues: Symmetric-part eigenvalues are positive and below one: 0.481–0.970 overall, and 0.672–0.938 for layers 26–28. This is consistent with anisotropic attenuation within each fitted subspace; it does not identify what features were attenuated.
conclusions.common_operator_hypothesis: A single unchanged physical rank-5 operator across layers 25–28 is not supported by these samples: pairwise Frobenius cosines are 0.157–0.602, and cross-layer predictions leave 88.20–131.12% of target-delta norm unexplained. Even refitting M within another layer's fixed U leaves 78.61–97.85% held-out residual. Adjacent layers can share partial subspace overlap without sharing the complete operator.
conclusions.bf16_rounding: Rounding the simple fitted predictions to BF16 and then the F16 export representation increases in-sample error energy by 37.35–42.70%, yielding 7.495–9.155% relative delta residual. Held-out results are similar. Thus this particular fitted prediction plus one rounding step does not account for the remaining residual, despite all observed target entries being BF16-representable. It does not rule out an earlier low-rank BF16 edit with unknown exact factors or a different construction path.
conclusions.smallest_next_diagnostic: Use same-layer attention output 27 first: freeze its recovered shared-down U, fit only attention coefficients on half the columns and evaluate the other half, compare against the attention-specific rank-5 spectral floor and matched Q8 null. Layer 25 is a useful second sample because its coefficient spectrum differs. The artifact agent owns that separately authorized Q8 pilot.
conclusions.exploratory_transfer_limit: Any future transfer should preserve layer-specific U and component-specific coefficient estimates, remain reversible, and be labeled exploratory. No common global operator, refusal-specific mechanism, REDCELL quality improvement, or transfer success has been established.
